events.title: Connecticut Ratifies the U.S. Constitution
events.description: Connecticut voted 128 to 40 to ratify the United States Constitution, becoming the fifth state to join the Union.
events.significance: Added momentum to the ratification campaign that brought the new federal government into being, replacing the weaker Articles of Confederation.

events.title: First Balloon Flight in North America
events.description: French aeronaut Jean-Pierre Blanchard flew a hydrogen balloon from Philadelphia and landed in Gloucester County, New Jersey, with President George Washington among the spectators.
events.significance: Marked the beginning of human flight in North America and showed early public fascination with aviation.

events.title: Bloody Sunday in St. Petersburg
events.description: Imperial troops fired on peaceful workers marching to petition Tsar Nicholas II for better conditions, killing and wounding hundreds. The date is January 22 in the Gregorian calendar but January 9 in the Julian calendar then used in Russia.
events.significance: Triggered the Russian Revolution of 1905 and severely damaged the Tsar's standing with the Russian people, foreshadowing the revolutions of 1917.

events.title: Birth of Richard Nixon
events.description: Richard Milhous Nixon, later the 37th President of the United States, was born in Yorba Linda, California.
events.significance: Nixon opened relations with China and pursued détente with the Soviet Union, but became the only U.S. president to resign, over the Watergate scandal in 1974.

events.title: Steve Jobs Unveils the iPhone
events.description: At the Macworld Conference in San Francisco, Apple CEO Steve Jobs introduced the first iPhone, combining a phone, an iPod and an internet communicator.
events.significance: Transformed the mobile industry and helped usher in the modern smartphone era, reshaping communication, media and commerce worldwide.
